title: Lace panel baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with a central eyelet panel in DK on 4 mm needles.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with a central twenty-stitch eyelet lace panel flanked by seed-stitch borders, worked in DK on 4 mm needles. The eyelet panel introduces yarn-overs and decreases in a simple four-row repeat. About 250 g of DK.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 5th series (1889), §Knitted Lace Baby Squares, gives a central eyelet panel cot blanket in double-knitting weight. The basic eyelet four-row repeat is documented in Mary Thomas's Book of Knitting Patterns (1943), §Simple Eyelet Patterns.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in seed stitch on 4 mm needles, unblocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small decorative hole formed by a yarn over paired with a decrease. The yarn over creates an extra stitch (the hole), and the decrease removes one stitch, keeping the total stitch count constant. Arranged in rows or columns, eyelets produce a lacy effect without requiring complex pattern reading.

A left-slanting decrease. Slip two stitches knitwise one at a time, then insert the left needle through the fronts of both slipped stitches and knit them together. The result is one stitch that leans to the left, mirroring a k2tog which leans to the right.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long. A twenty-stitch central
eyelet
panel sits between two seed-stitch side borders.

A single panel avoids seaming. Seed stitch borders were chosen because seed stitch lies flat without blocking and frames the lace panel without a visible structural border. The eyelet panel uses yarn-over increases paired with
ssk
and k2tog decreases in a simple four-row repeat. The overall fabric does not curl. Budget about 250 g (about 550 m / 600 yards) of machine-washable DK. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 250 g (about 550 m / 600 yards) of DK-weight machine-washable yarn. A smooth plied DK shows eyelets more clearly than a bouclé or textured yarn.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Blocking mat and pins
items.qty: Optional, blocking opens the eyelets considerably

content.text: Gauge
22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in seed stitch on 4 mm needles. The eyelet panel sits slightly open; the seed stitch gauge drives the blanket width.
If your gauge is 20 stitches per 10 cm with 166 stitches on the needle, the blanket will be about 83 cm wide. Adjust the seed-stitch side panels in multiples of 2 to hit your target width.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 166 stitches (73 seed + 20 eyelet panel + 73 seed). Long-tail tail: (4 × 166) / 10 + 15 = 66.4 + 15 = 81 cm. Measure 95 cm of tail. Place markers after stitch 73 and before stitch 94 to mark the eyelet panel.
Body
All rows outside markers: seed stitch (k the purls, p the knits).
Eyelet panel, row 1 (RS): k2, *yo, k2tog; repeat from * to last 2 sts of panel, k2.
Eyelet panel, row 2 (WS): p20.
Eyelet panel, row 3 (RS): k2, *ssk, yo; repeat from * to last 2 sts of panel, k2.
Eyelet panel, row 4 (WS): p20.
Repeat these 4 panel rows until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note which of the four panel rows is next.
Stitch count check-ins
At row 135 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 166 stitches: 73 in each seed panel and 20 in the eyelet panel. At row 268 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults
Stitch count drifting upward: a yo was placed without a matching decrease, or two yo were placed in one position. Count stitches in the panel at the end of each RS row during the first repeat.
Eyelets appearing as closed bumps rather than open holes: the yarn was not brought fully over the needle before the next stitch. Check that the yarn forms a complete loop over the needle on each yo.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern: seed stitch panels cast off alternating k and p; eyelet panel cast off knitwise. Use a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in both ends. Wet block the finished piece to open the eyelets: pin to measurements on a blocking mat and leave to dry fully. The seed stitch will also relax and even out after blocking.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry, reshaping to measurements.
What to try next

From a central eyelet panel, try an all-over eyelet blanket next. Use the same four-row repeat across the full width. You already know every technique required. The result is an open, lacy fabric throughout.
